get.description:
Public health endpoint aggregating gateway, worker, and database status.

Under the armed desktop profile this ungated surface discloses only the
minimal liveness signal - no process identity, service identity, or product
state crosses the unauthenticated boundary; the aggregate readiness facts move
behind attach authentication on the service-state verb and the authenticated
liveness surface. The Compose and development profiles retain the full
aggregate body their gateway healthchecks already consume.

post.description: Create a new orchestration thread and dispatch to the worker.

get.description: List orchestration threads with pagination and optional status filter.
Return the full ThreadMetadata object for a thread.

delete.description:
Delete a thread through the durable cross-store deletion saga.

A replayed request resumes the same saga rather than starting a second
teardown, so repeated calls converge on one deletion.

The service result distinguishes more states than a two-code surface can
carry, so this verb answers with five outcomes: a lifecycle refusal before
the saga begins, a clean deletion, a deletion that finalized over
unremovable cleanup state, resumable incomplete cleanup, and an
already-absent thread.

200.description: Deleted, but cleanup was abandoned over permanently unremovable state; the body names the kinds left behind.

409.description: The thread's lifecycle state refuses deletion.

503.description: Cleanup is unfinished but resumable; retry.

post.description: Transition a thread to ARCHIVED status.

get.description: Stream thread events over SSE for clients that do not use WebSockets.

Return a complete thread state snapshot for client reconnection.

The ``last_sequence`` field enables gap detection: the client discards
any subsequent WebSocket events with ``sequence <= last_sequence``.

post.description:
Send a user message into an existing thread.

Returns 202 Accepted immediately; the message is dispatched to the
worker process for graph execution.
Cancel a running thread by dispatching a cancel action to the worker.

get.description: Return current team status: agents, active threads, pending permissions.
Return all available team presets for the team picker UI.

post.description: Submit a permission response via REST for guaranteed delivery.

Initiate graceful server shutdown.

Administrative shutdown is a receipt-bound lifecycle operation: it requires
both authenticated runtime control (the attach credential) and receipt
ownership (the lifecycle capability that discovery never references), so a
foreign attachment that can reach the product surface still cannot stop the
gateway.

Run admission is closed first, so the gateway admits no new run while it
drains; the in-process stop is then deferred briefly so this 202 flushes
before the SIGINT-driven graceful shutdown - which drains and reaps the owned
worker and run descendants in the lifespan - begins.

schema.title: Response Shutdown Endpoint Api Admin Shutdown Post

post.description:
Start, prepare, commit, or release through the single run-start verb.

The ``stage`` selector splits one verb into four shapes without growing the
verb set: ``prepare`` reserves bounded capacity without tokens or a durable
run; ``commit`` binds the exact actor-token role set to that reservation;
``release`` frees only an uncommitted reservation; and ``start`` (the
default) preserves the one-shot engine/Compose path.

schema.title: Response Run Start Endpoint V1 Runs Post

get.description: Return a capped identity projection for durable non-terminal runs.
Return the authoritative recovery snapshot for a run.

delete.description:
Delete a run through the durable cross-store deletion saga.

A replayed request resumes the same saga rather than starting a second
teardown, so repeated calls converge on one deletion.

Five outcomes, because the service distinguishes more states than two codes
can carry: a lifecycle refusal before the saga begins, a clean deletion, a
deletion that finalized over unremovable state, resumable incomplete
cleanup, and an already-absent run. The retryable code is reserved for the
genuinely resumable case - the abandoned case is terminal, and inviting a
retry there would send the caller to a not-found.

200.description: Deleted, but cleanup was abandoned over permanently unremovable state; the body names the kinds left behind.

409.description: The run's lifecycle state refuses deletion.

503.description: Cleanup is unfinished but resumable; retry.

get.description:
Re-serve the run's bounded, versioned v1 SSE progress frames.

The public streaming companion to run-status: run-status is the authoritative
recovery snapshot, this is the droppable live progress relay. A run id is the
thread id, so this delegates to the same stream builder the internal
``/api/threads/{id}/stream`` route uses - one code path, the same versioned
256 KiB-bounded frames, the same terminal-replay-then-close semantics. Frames
are non-authoritative by contract: a consumer reconciles run state from
run-status, never from a relay frame.

post.description:
Move a terminal run to the archived state.

Archiving is not deletion: the run and its records survive, marked
historical. A run whose state does not permit archiving is refused rather
than silently ignored, and repeating the call on an already-archived run is
that same refusal - the conflict IS the replay signal here.

get.description:
Report the team's live operational projection.

A read, and deliberately a narrow one: which agents exist and what state
they are in, which runs are active, and what is awaiting an answer. It
carries no prompt, no document body, and no credential - the same
disclosure discipline the progress channel holds.

post.description:
Send a follow-up turn into an existing run.

Run-start cannot carry this. A repeat run identifier there is a REPLAY - it
answers with the original run and never adopts the new body - so without
this verb the versioned surface can start a run and watch it, but never say
anything further to it.

Accepted is not applied: the turn is handed to the worker and execution
continues asynchronously, so a caller reconciles from the stream or
run-status rather than from this response.

Answer a permission request the run raised on its progress stream.

The versioned surface already POSES this question - ``permission_request``
is an enumerated frame on run-stream - and this is where the answer returns.
Without it the only answering channel is the transition surface, so retiring
that surface would strand every paused run.

The verb adds no state machine of its own: it is a versioned projection of
the same answer path, so at-most-once behaviour comes from there. Answering
twice replays the stored outcome rather than acting again, an answer arriving
after the request was applied reports the duplicate without re-dispatching,
and a superseded or expired request is refused with a journaled rejection
that replays identically.

Scoping matters as much as the answer. The request is resolved and checked
against the run in the path BEFORE anything acts on it, so a guessed request
id cannot be used to answer another run's question - and because that check
precedes the service call, a mismatch has no effect at all rather than being
detected after the fact.

get.description:
List team presets truthfully, marking each loadable or unloadable.

Resolution uses the requested workspace context so workspace-local presets
are listed alongside the bundled set. A single preset that fails to load or
validate is reported with ``loadable=False`` and a reason rather than
omitted or allowed to crash the whole listing. Each loadable preset carries
its model profiles with per-role effective assignments (resolved by the same
shared resolver launch uses) and backend-computed eligibility. The whole
build - file I/O, provider readiness, and the engine reachability probe -
runs off the event loop.

Return truthful, probe-backed readiness for the resident gateway.

Runs the real dependency probes (database, checkpoint, worker) rather than
reporting a hardcoded status, and separates process-alive from
can-accept-run. Engine authoring-backend reachability is reported from
non-blocking discovery-file freshness.
Readiness probe -- confirms the internal API is accepting connections.

schema.title: Response Internal Health Internal Health Get

post.description:
Receive a single event from the worker and relay to browser clients.

The ``WorkerBridge`` in the worker process POSTs here instead of
sending a WebSocket frame.  The payload format matches
``WorkerEventEnvelope``.

schema.title: Response Receive Worker Event Internal Events Post

post.description:
Receive a batch of events from the worker.

The ``WorkerBridge`` accumulates events for a short interval then
POSTs them as a single ``{"events": [...]}`` payload.  Each entry
has the same shape as a single-event envelope (``thread_id`` +
``payload``).

schema.title: Response Receive Worker Event Batch Internal Events Batch Post

post.description:
Receive a heartbeat from the worker.

Updates ``app.state`` so the gateway can monitor worker
liveness without a persistent WebSocket connection.

schema.title: Response Receive Worker Heartbeat Internal Heartbeat Post

get.description:
Top-level liveness check for external probes.

Under the armed desktop profile the unauthenticated boundary discloses
only the minimal liveness fact - no process identity, product identity, or
product state - while an attach-authenticated caller additionally receives
the readiness projection from the single readiness authority. The Compose
and development profiles retain the legacy aggregate liveness body their
probes already consume; readiness there stays on `/api/health`.

ActiveRunRecord.title: ActiveRunRecord
ActiveRunRecord.description: Minimal durable run identity used to recover a viewing binding.

ActiveRunsResponse.title: ActiveRunsResponse
ActiveRunsResponse.description: Bounded, non-authoritative discovery result for active runs.

ActorTokenBundle.title: ActorTokenBundle
ActorTokenBundle.description:
A run's per-role actor tokens plus the engine machine bearer.

Parameters
----------
tokens:
    Mapping of role identifier (the worker ``agent_id`` or the supervisor
    constant) to that role's engine-minted actor token. A role only ever
    receives its own token via :meth:`actor_token`.
engine_bearer:
    The machine bearer minted at engine boot, forwarded so a worker's
    authoring bridge can reach the engine. Optional: when absent the worker
    resolves the bearer from the engine discovery file instead.

AgentLifecycleState.title: AgentLifecycleState
AgentLifecycleState.description:
Observable agent states exposed to the frontend.

Maps to the MCP states. Tracks
internal process lifecycle (init/ready/running/error/done).

AgentStatusEntry.title: AgentStatusEntry
AgentStatusEntry.description:
Wire projection of the canonical agent descriptor for ``/team/status``.

Mirrors ``thread.snapshots.AgentData``.

CleanupKind.title: CleanupKind
CleanupKind.description:
The kind of thread-owned state one deletion cleanup item removes.

Deliberately a kind and never a locator: it names *what class of state* a
delete touched, so both the durable cleanup manifest and the delete
response can speak it, while the concrete checkpoint id or artifact path
stays inside the control plane.

ContextRef.title: ContextRef
ContextRef.description: Reference to a context document in the .vault hierarchy.

CreateThreadResponse.title: CreateThreadResponse
CreateThreadResponse.description: Response after successfully creating a thread.

DeleteThreadResponse.title: DeleteThreadResponse
DeleteThreadResponse.description:
Report a deletion that finished while leaving external state stranded.

A delete answers with no content when every store was cleaned. This body is
returned instead when the deletion finalized over at least one cleanup item
judged permanently unremovable: the thread is durably gone - retrying would
answer not-found - but some state outside the control database was left
behind and a client reconciling against this surface would otherwise read
the thread as cleanly deleted.

``abandoned_kinds`` names *what* was stranded so the fact is actionable.
The concrete targets are deliberately absent: a checkpoint id or an artifact
path is control-plane state, not the caller's to receive.

DesktopReadiness.title: DesktopReadiness
DesktopReadiness.description:
The authenticated desktop readiness projection.

Carries process and product identity alongside the five separate bounded
readiness facts. The facts are never collapsed into a single boolean: a cold,
startable worker leaves ``gateway_readiness`` ``ready`` while ``run_admission``
stays ``deferred``, so gateway-readiness and execution-readiness remain
distinct. Served only to an attach-authenticated caller.

ExecutionTaskSnapshot.title: ExecutionTaskSnapshot
ExecutionTaskSnapshot.description: Normalized execution task used in reconnect snapshots.

GatewayReadiness.title: GatewayReadiness
GatewayReadiness.description:
Whether a live gateway with a valid database is ready to be attached.

Independent of worker state: a live gateway with a valid database and a cold,
startable worker is ``ready``. A gateway-owned dependency failure - an invalid
or unreachable database - is ``not_ready``.

LivenessState.title: LivenessState
LivenessState.description:
Minimal process-liveness fact: the gateway answered, or it did not.

This is the only fact an unauthenticated caller ever observes. It proves
neither ownership nor readiness and discloses no product state.

MessageSnapshot.title: MessageSnapshot
MessageSnapshot.description: Fully materialized message in a thread replay.

Model.title: Model
Model.description:
LLM capability levels.

Abstracts specific version strings to reduce maintenance burden.

PermissionOptionKind.title: PermissionOptionKind
PermissionOptionKind.description:
User permission response options (mirrors ACP PermissionOption.kind).

Values:
    ALLOW_ONCE: Allow the tool call this time only.
    ALLOW_ALWAYS: Allow all future invocations of this tool without prompting.
    REJECT_ONCE: Deny the tool call this time only.
    REJECT_ALWAYS: Deny all future invocations of this tool without prompting.

PermissionResponseRequest.title: PermissionResponseRequest
PermissionResponseRequest.description: Submit a permission response via REST (guaranteed delivery).

PermissionResponseResult.title: PermissionResponseResult
PermissionResponseResult.description: Result of submitting a permission response.

PlanEntry.title: PlanEntry
PlanEntry.description:
A single entry in the agent's execution plan.

Fields use plain ``str`` so the domain layer stays free of wire-protocol
enum imports.  Values correspond to ``PlanEntryStatus`` / ``PlanEntryPriority``
members defined in ``api.schemas.enums``.

PresetSummary.title: PresetSummary
PresetSummary.description:
One discovered team preset and whether it is actually runnable.

A preset whose TOML is missing or invalid is still listed with
``loadable=False`` and an ``unavailable_reason`` so the Rust backend sees the
truthful set rather than a listing that omits or crashes on it. Descriptive
fields are populated only when the preset loaded.

ProfileSummary.title: ProfileSummary
ProfileSummary.description:
One selectable model profile for a preset.

Carries the profile's identity, whether it is the default, its per-role
effective assignments (resolved by the same shared resolver launch uses, so
picker truth cannot drift from execution truth), and backend-computed
eligibility with safe reasons.

ProviderEligibility.title: ProviderEligibility
ProviderEligibility.description:
Whether at least one subprocess provider command resolves on this host.

Computed through the no-instantiation classify seam: no provider is
constructed and no subprocess is spawned to determine it.

RoleAssignmentSummary.title: RoleAssignmentSummary
RoleAssignmentSummary.description:
Effective per-role model assignment under a profile.

Only safe operational metadata: role id, agent id, provider id, capability,
the stable concrete model name, ordered fallbacks, current provider readiness,
and which precedence layer the assignment came from. Never a credential, env
value, token, or private path.

RoleState.title: RoleState
RoleState.description: Per-role lifecycle state within a run (recovery snapshot).

RunAdmission.title: RunAdmission
RunAdmission.description:
Whether the gateway would admit a run right now - the execution-ready fact.

``ready`` means execution-ready: a reachable worker and an eligible provider.
``deferred`` means gateway-ready but not yet execution-ready - the worker is
cold or starting and will start on demand. It remains informational on the
readiness surface, while staged ``prepare`` admission refuses it fail-closed.
``blocked`` means a hard gateway dependency (the database) is unavailable.

RunAgentSummary.title: RunAgentSummary
RunAgentSummary.description: One agent's disclosed operational state in the team projection.

RunArchiveResponse.title: RunArchiveResponse
RunArchiveResponse.description: Acknowledge a run moved to the archived state.

RunCommitResponse.title: RunCommitResponse
RunCommitResponse.description:
Acknowledge a run committed against a prepared reservation.

Returned by the ``commit`` stage. The reservation is consumed and a stable
run is created and dispatched with the bound actor tokens. ``lease_id`` is the
non-secret, run-scoped lease identity the dashboard revokes at terminal
settlement; it is an identifier, never a bearer.

RunDeleteResponse.title: RunDeleteResponse
RunDeleteResponse.description:
Report a deletion that finalized over state no pass could remove.

Carried only on that one outcome. A clean deletion answers with no body at
all, so the presence of this body IS the signal that external state was
stranded. Names the KINDS of item left behind and nothing more: a concrete
checkpoint id or artifact path is control-plane state and never the
caller's to receive.

RunMessageRequest.title: RunMessageRequest
RunMessageRequest.description:
Send a follow-up turn into a run that already exists.

Run-start cannot express this: a repeat run identifier is a REPLAY, answered
with the original run, so there is no way to say "same run, new input"
through it. This is that verb.

RunMessageResponse.title: RunMessageResponse
RunMessageResponse.description:
Acknowledge a follow-up turn as accepted for dispatch.

Acceptance is not completion: the turn is handed to the worker and the run
continues asynchronously, so a caller reconciles progress from the stream or
run-status rather than from this body.

RunPendingPermission.title: RunPendingPermission
RunPendingPermission.description: A permission awaiting an answer, addressed by the run that raised it.

RunPermissionRespondRequest.title: RunPermissionRespondRequest
RunPermissionRespondRequest.description:
Answer one permission request raised by a run.

Carries only the chosen option. The options themselves were advertised on
the versioned progress stream in the ``permission_request`` frame that
raised the question, so the answer names one rather than restating it.

RunPermissionRespondResponse.title: RunPermissionRespondResponse
RunPermissionRespondResponse.description:
Report what an answer did, including when it did nothing.

``accepted`` says the answer was taken; ``applied`` says it was the one that
resumed the run. A duplicate answer reports accepted with ``applied`` false
rather than acting twice, so a caller that retries after a lost response
learns the outcome instead of re-answering.

RunPrepareResponse.title: RunPrepareResponse
RunPrepareResponse.description:
Acknowledge a prepared admission reservation.

Returned by the ``prepare`` stage of run-start. It carries the server-minted
reservation identity a later ``commit`` binds to, its non-secret run-scoped
lease identity, the bounded validated set of roles that commit's actor-token
bundle must cover, and the reservation's hard expiry. The three readiness
facts report why admission is or is not
execution-ready right now. No durable run exists yet and no token was
accepted; a reservation that is never committed simply expires.

RunReleaseResponse.title: RunReleaseResponse
RunReleaseResponse.description: Acknowledge explicit release of an uncommitted reservation.

RunStage.title: RunStage
RunStage.description:
Which stage of the run-start verb a request drives.

The single ``POST /v1/runs`` verb supports ``prepare`` for readiness-gated,
expiring capacity; ``commit`` for exact request and actor-role binding;
``release`` for an uncommitted reservation; and the pre-existing one-shot
``start`` compatibility path.

RunStartRequest.title: RunStartRequest
RunStartRequest.description:
Start a run: the engine-facing shape of thread-create + first message.

Carries the engine-provisioned per-role actor token bundle alongside
the run's preset and opening message. The gateway threads this onto the same
dispatch path the internal thread-create flow uses — no second code path.

RunStartResponse.title: RunStartResponse
RunStartResponse.description: Acknowledge a started run, with its initial semantic status.

RunStatusResponse.title: RunStatusResponse
RunStatusResponse.description:
The authoritative recovery snapshot for a run.

Designed as the read a restarted A2A resumes or reports a run from: topology
position, per-role state, and the engine proposal/changeset ids the run has
produced, plus the checkpoint cursor and repair posture. Non-authoritative
SSE progress frames may be lost freely; this snapshot is the source of truth.

SendMessageRequest.title: SendMessageRequest
SendMessageRequest.description: Send a user message into an existing thread via REST.

SendMessageResponse.title: SendMessageResponse
SendMessageResponse.description: Response after accepting a user message (202 Accepted).

ServiceStateResponse.title: ServiceStateResponse
ServiceStateResponse.description:
Backend-served readiness for the A2A service (service-state verb).

Distinguishes three truths the Rust backend must not conflate: the process is
``alive`` (it answered), the service ``can_accept_run`` (dependencies are
ready), and - separately, via presets-list eligibility - whether a chosen
authoring preset is runnable. A live HTTP process is not evidence that a run
can start, so ``status`` is derived from real dependency probes rather than
hardcoded.

TeamPresetSummary.title: TeamPresetSummary
TeamPresetSummary.description: Lightweight team preset descriptor for the team picker UI.

TeamPresetsResponse.title: TeamPresetsResponse
TeamPresetsResponse.description: Response for GET /teams: list of available team presets.

TeamStatusResponse.title: TeamStatusResponse
TeamStatusResponse.description: Current team status snapshot via REST.

TeamStatusV1Response.title: TeamStatusV1Response
TeamStatusV1Response.description:
The team's live operational projection.

Safe operational metadata only - which agents exist, what state they are in,
which runs are active, and what is awaiting an answer. Never a credential,
a prompt, or a document body.

ThreadMetadata.title: ThreadMetadata
ThreadMetadata.description: Provenance and context attached to an orchestration thread.

ThreadStateSnapshot.title: ThreadStateSnapshot
ThreadStateSnapshot.description:
Complete thread state for reconnection replay.

The client fetches this via REST, notes ``last_sequence``, then
discards any WebSocket events with ``sequence <= last_sequence``.

ThreadStatus.title: ThreadStatus
ThreadStatus.description: Durable lifecycle states for orchestration threads.

ThreadSummary.title: ThreadSummary
ThreadSummary.description: Lightweight thread descriptor for list endpoints.

ToolCallContentDiff.title: ToolCallContentDiff
ToolCallContentDiff.description: Diff content block within a tool call.

ToolCallContentTerminal.title: ToolCallContentTerminal
ToolCallContentTerminal.description: Terminal output content block within a tool call.

ToolCallContentText.title: ToolCallContentText
ToolCallContentText.description: Plain text content block within a tool call.

ToolCallLocation.title: ToolCallLocation
ToolCallLocation.description: File location associated with a tool call.

ToolCallSnapshot.title: ToolCallSnapshot
ToolCallSnapshot.description: Fully materialized tool call (all incremental updates merged).

ToolCallStatus.title: ToolCallStatus
ToolCallStatus.description: Lifecycle states for a single tool invocation.

TopologyPosition.title: TopologyPosition
TopologyPosition.description:
Where a run sits in its team topology (recovery snapshot).

Product-facing status speaks role vocabulary only: ``active_agent`` is
the role currently working, never an internal LangGraph node name. The raw
next-node projection lives in the internal recovery snapshot
(``thread/snapshots.py``), not this contract; ``next_nodes`` was dropped
from the v1 surface.

WorkerLifecycleState.title: WorkerLifecycleState
WorkerLifecycleState.description:
The gateway-owned worker's rung on the cold-to-execution ladder.

``cold`` is the pre-demand resting state: no worker exists yet and one is
startable on first execution demand. It is informational, never degradation.
``starting`` is the single-flight startup window, ``ready`` is an up and
reachable worker, and ``unavailable`` is a worker that started but is down or
restarting after demand.

_AgentSnapshot.title: _AgentSnapshot
_AgentSnapshot.description:
Wire projection of the canonical agent descriptor within a snapshot.

Mirrors ``thread.snapshots.AgentData``.

_PermissionSnapshot.title: _PermissionSnapshot
_PermissionSnapshot.description: Outstanding permission request in a state snapshot.
